evidence_span.text: Sterol regulatory element-binding proteins (SREBPs), master transcriptional regulators of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis, have been found to contribute to a diverse array of cellular processes. In this review, we focus on genetically engineered mice in which the activities of six components of the SREBP gene pathway, namely SREBP-1, SREBP-2, Scap, Insig-1, Insig-2, or Site-1 protease have been altered through gene knockout or transgenic approaches.

reviews.rationale: This review names Scap/Insig-1 as SREBP-pathway master regulators (perturbation regulators, not supplied genes) but gives no regulatory direction and no data on supplied genes Erg28/Rdh11, and is framed around extrahepatic/developmental functions. Declared direct context is overclaimed for a secondary, extrahepatic synthesis.

evidence_span.text: The combination of an SQS inhibitor with an HMGCR or FDPS inhibitor provides a rational approach for reducing cholesterol synthesis while preventing nonsterol isoprenoid depletion.

reviews.rationale: Novel squalene-synthase (Fdft1) inhibitors reduce cholesterol biosynthesis in HepG2 cells, and the FDPS inhibitor zoledronate is experimentally used showing FDPS's FPP-synthase role upstream of cholesterol synthesis, so both genes have gene-specific causal support. HepG2 is a transferable hepatic context, matching the declared partial label.

evidence_span.text: Conversely, the direct product of CYP51 demethylation, follicular fluid meiosis-activating sterol (FF-MAS), was decreased 2.6- and 2.1-fold in 6-week HCyp51−/− mice and runts, respectively.

reviews.rationale: Hepatocyte-specific Cyp51 knockout causally lowers the CYP51 demethylation product FF-MAS and causes progressive liver injury, directly supporting its biosynthetic enzyme role. The model is a developmental (pubertal) mouse liver rather than the aging/MASLD condition, so the declared direct context is overclaimed.

evidence_span.text: Taken together, many genes play a central role in cholesterol synthesis, including HMGCR, SQLE, HMGCS1, FDFT1, LSS, MVK, PMK, MVD, FDPS, CYP51, TM7SF2, LBR, MSMO1, NSDHL, HSD17B7, DHCR24, EBP, SC5D, DHCR7, IDI1/2 (Fig. 1).

reviews.rationale: This circRNA/miRNA review only catalogs the pathway genes from KEGG in background text without gene-specific investigation, so no gene qualifies as studied, but it secondarily supports the general claim that these are cholesterol-biosynthesis enzymes. 'No' understated this and B's 15 function-supported genes overclaimed pathway-list mentions.
